events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.72)
events.body:
The ride was a metered RydeTAXI trip, so the fare follows the meter rather than the quote: total $45.04 comprises base $3.90, distance $30.46 for 21.60 km, time $9.10 for 35.0 min, waiting $0.11 and platform $1.47, with no surge [F7][F6]. Any refund therefore turns on RD-2, whose non-metered branch does not apply and whose metered branch pays only for unexempt off-route segments [RD-2].

There is a single off-route segment, the 09:20–09:26 loop that drove 4.04 km where the optimal route covers 1.86 km, adding 2.18 km and straying up to 1027 m from the optimal route [F3]; the trip-wide +2.3 km against 19.3 km optimal is that same segment [F1]. RD-1 is engaged: no percentage or absolute threshold exists, and every such segment must be reviewed under RD-3 / RD-4 / RD-5 [RD-1].

RD-4 does not excuse it. No traffic incident was recorded near the optimal route in the trip window [F15], and the only congestion record on the optimal route — EAST COAST PARKWAY at speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) during 08:58–09:20 [F12] — is corroborative only and cannot stand alone as an exemption [RD-4]. The driver's post-trip explanation that he "went round" because traffic was building [F11] is a statement, not the traffic evidence RD-4(a) requires [RD-4].

The decisive question is RD-5, the rider's consent, and the trace leaves it to me. The driver asked at 09:17 whether to take another way because of ECP congestion [F8], and the rider replied at 09:18: "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late." [F9], two minutes before the segment started at 09:20 [F3]. The chat record is complete and every message timestamped [F10], so consent is properly evidenced by the rider's own message sent before the segment [RD-5]. Those words are the policy's own example of a general route authorisation — "take whichever way is faster" [RD-5]. A general route choice covers the route chosen to reach the destination, and the alternative that the rider's authorisation selected is consistent with the recorded conditions: the corridor the driver named was slow (ECP band 2, 10–19 km/h) [F12][F8] while the airport corridor was free-flowing (AIRPORT BOULEVARD band 5, 40–49 km/h) [F13]; no incident and fair weather remove any other branch [F15][F16]. The segment is therefore exempt and adds nothing refundable.

The metered waiting unit of $0.11 for 0.4 min is chargeable on a RydeTAXI trip and is not refundable [F5][RD-3]. The billed excess of $3.31 for 2.35 km [F4] is not refundable either, since it is the price of the exempt segment and of corridor variation RD-2 does not restore [RD-2].

RD-6's add-on does not arise: the execution trace marks the prior-upheld-route-dispute element ✗, the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days, and no RD-1 breach or RD-2 refund is recorded against him here, so no flag_account is set [F18][RD-6]. RD-1 is engaged: no percentage or absolute threshold exists, and every such segment must be reviewed under RD-3 / RD-4 / RD-5 [RD-1].

RD-4 does not excuse it. No traffic incident was recorded near the optimal route in the trip window [F15], and the only congestion record on the optimal route — EAST COAST PARKWAY at speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) during 08:58–09:20 [F12] — is corroborative only and cannot stand alone as an exemption [RD-4]. The driver's post-trip explanation that he "went round" because traffic was building [F11] is a statement, not the traffic evidence RD-4(a) requires [RD-4].

The decisive question is RD-5, the rider's consent, and the trace leaves it to me. The driver asked at 09:17 whether to take another way because of ECP congestion [F8], and the rider replied at 09:18: "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late." [F9], two minutes before the segment started at 09:20 [F3]. The chat record is complete and every message timestamped [F10], so consent is properly evidenced by the rider's own message sent before the segment [RD-5]. Those words are the policy's own example of a general route authorisation — "take whichever way is faster" [RD-5]. A general route choice covers the route chosen to reach the destination, and the alternative that the rider's authorisation selected is consistent with the recorded conditions: the corridor the driver named was slow (ECP band 2, 10–19 km/h) [F12][F8] while the airport corridor was free-flowing (AIRPORT BOULEVARD band 5, 40–49 km/h) [F13]; no incident and fair weather remove any other branch [F15][F16]. There is exactly one off-route segment, 09:20–09:26, where 4.04 km were driven over road the optimal route covers in 1.86 km, adding 2.18 km and straying up to 1027 m from the optimal route (F3); no RD-3 or RD-4 exemption covers it, so it is an unexcused deviation under RD-1.

The only rider message before the segment is 'Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late.' at 09:18 (F9), 2 minutes before the segment started at 09:20 (F3); that is a general route authorisation to reach the destination, not consent to a 2.18 km detour, and it does not cover a loop that the record does not show to be faster.

The driver's justification fails RD-4: the only congestion record on the optimal route is EAST COAST PARKWAY band 2 ending at 09:20 (F12), which alone is not a basis for exemption, and no traffic incident at all was recorded near the route in the trip window (F15); the driver's post-trip statement that traffic was 'building up ahead' (F11) is a statement, not the traffic evidence RD-4 requires.

Because RydeTAXI is metered on distance, the refund under RD-2 is the unexcused segment's extra_km at this trip's per-km rate: 2.18 km × $1.4102/km = $3.07 (rounded to the cent), taken from the segment's 2.18 km extra (F3) and the rate in F4 ($1.4102/km, distance fare ÷ distance km).

The billed excess distance of 2.35 km ($3.31) also exceeds the 2.18 km actually added by the segment (F3, F4); the 0.17 km difference is corridor noise that RD-2 leaves unrestored, so the claim is limited to the segment's own 2.18 km.
The 0.4 min / $0.11 waiting charge (F5) is a metered in-trip waiting unit on a RydeTAXI trip and is not refundable under RD-3(c); there is no claim here for it.

The driver has 3 disputes with 2 upheld in the last 90 days (F18), and since this case establishes a route-deviation breach, RD-6 asks the court to add flag_account so Ryde reviews the account; the profile facts are offered only for that additional action, not to prove the deviation itself.

weaknesses: The rider did say 'Just take whichever way is faster lah' at 09:18 (F9), before the segment began at 09:20 (F3); the driver will argue this general authorisation covers the reroute, and the only way we defeat it is by showing the segment was not faster — EAST COAST PARKWAY was only band 2 (10–19 km/h) and the alternative was not congestion-free either (F12, F13, F14), with no incident recorded (F15).

The record contains no road name for the driven segment (F3 gives only distance and deviation), so if the judge reads F9 as an agreement to a specific route rather than a general choice, the segment falls to named_road_untied / undetermined and the matter would go to a human under RD-5 rather than be decided here.

The trip did arrive (drop-off 09:42) and the meter difference is small — billed excess $3.31 against a $45.04 fare (F4, F7); the driver will say the +12% distance was negligible against a genuine airport run and that the rider, who is late, accepted the trade-off by messaging F9.
